name: Question 4
problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.35$ |
| $X=6$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ |

Which of the following gives the covariance of $X$ and $Y?$
worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.35$ | $0.55$ |
| $X=6$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =2\cdot 0.25+4\cdot 0.55+6\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.5+2.2+1.2 \\  & =3.9 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =2\cdot 0.4+4\cdot 0.6 \\  & =0.8+2.4 \\  & =3.2\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-3.9)(y-3.2)f(x,y).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

The joint probability mass function f(x,y) for the discrete random variables X and Y with joint support S=SX×SY is given below.

f Y=2 Y=4
X=2 0.15 0.1
X=4 0.2 0.35
X=6 0.05 0.15

Which of the following gives the covariance of X and Y?

a
∑(x,y)∈S(x−3.9)(y−3.2)f(x,y)
b
 ∑(x,y)∈S(x−3.2)(y−3.9)f(x,y)
c
 ∑(x,y)∈S(xy−3)f(x,y)
d
 ∑(x,y)∈Sx(y−3)f(x,y)
e
 ∑(x,y)∈S(x−4)(y−3)f(x,y)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The covariance of two discrete random variables X and Y with joint support S is defined as

Cov[X,Y]=∑(x,y)∈S(x−E[X])(y−E[Y])f(x,y).

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for X and Y. These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

f Y=2 Y=4 fX
X=2 0.15 0.1 0.25
X=4 0.2 0.35 0.55
X=6 0.05 0.15 0.2
fY 0.4 0.6 1

We now compute E[X] and E[Y], as follows:

E[X]=∑x∈SXx⋅fX(x)=2⋅0.25+4⋅0.55+6⋅0.2=0.5+2.2+1.2=3.9E[Y]=∑y∈SYy⋅fY(y)=2⋅0.4+4⋅0.6=0.8+2.4=3.2

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

Cov[X,Y]=∑(x,y)∈S(x−E[X])(y−E[Y])f(x,y)=∑(x,y)∈S(x−3.9)(y−3.2)f(x,y).
